items.title: El Niño Could Push Up Food Prices in Southern Africa
items.content: <article>Absa AgriBusiness agricultural economist Zama Sangweni says El Niño could reduce summer crop yields and put upward pressure on food prices. She explains how more severe weather could also reshape regional trade and why countries including Zambia may be especially exposed through agriculture, employment and hydropower. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: China Dispatches Pair of Pandas to Atlanta Zoo: CCTV Reports
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s giant pandas Pingping and Fushuang departed Chengdu for Zoo Atlanta early Sunday on a chartered flight, beginning a 10-year stay in the US, China Central Television reported on Sunday.</article>

items.title: Thai PM Anutin’s Support Drops in Latest Poll as Pressures Rise
items.author: Suttinee Yuvejwattana
items.content: <article>Public support for Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and his Bhumjaithai Party has plunged, according to an opinion poll, as his government confronts rising oil prices and a court ruling that may threaten its hold on power.</article>

items.title: Australia Home Auction Clearances Hit 10-Week Low as Rate Hike Looms
items.author: Ainsley Thomson
items.content: <article>Australia’s auction clearance rate declined to a 10-week low as a long weekend in Melbourne and the threat of higher borrowing costs weighed on sentiment.</article>

items.title: China’s Consumer Stocks Face Lost Decade as AI Steals Spotlight
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Under the shadow of Beijing’s single-minded focus on artificial intelligence, China’s consumer stocks are trapped in a lost decade.</article>

items.title: Bond Market Volatility Signals Risks for Corporate Debt Investors
items.author: Davide Barbuscia and Ronan Martin
items.content: <article>Corporate bonds have been relatively resilient amid a global government bond selloff, but the strength may not last.</article>

items.title: Bangladesh Targets Up to $1 Billion in Debut Sovereign Bond Sale
items.author: Arun Devnath
items.content: <article>Bangladesh is preparing to raise between $500 million and $1 billion through its maiden foreign-currency sovereign bond sale within the next three months, a senior government official said.</article>

items.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 09/26/2026
items.content: <article>The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by The New York Times Kyiv Bureau Chief Andrew Kramer, The Netherlands Prime Minister Rob Jetten, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists Editor-in-Chief and “The Valley of Death” Author Sharon Weinberger, Mexico Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Alvarez, ABC News State Department Reporter Shannon Kingston and Alphaville Editor and “A Fabulous Debt” Author Robin Wigglesworth. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
items.content: <article>Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Alexis Christoforous, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US and China Seek Common Ground on AI
items.content: <article>Bloomberg News Chief North Asia Correspondent Stephen Engle and ABC News State Department reporter Shannon Kingston tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping’s summit highlighted efforts to establish dialogue on AI while building trust between the two countries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle and Kingston examine the significance of Xi’s state visit, China’s push to be treated as an equal to the US and the diplomatic signals surrounding the meetings. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: How Syracuse's Semiconductor Gamble May Help Save the Rust Belt
items.content: <article>What does it actually take to bring a Rust Belt city back to life? Micron is building one of the largest semiconductor factories in US history in Syracuse, a city that experienced major job loss after companies including GE, Carrier and General Motors left the area. Rob Simpson of CenterState CEO explains what attracted Micron to the city, local business owner Darin Price talks about what the investment means on the ground, and Brookings economist Joseph Parilla makes the case that Syracuse could be a model for reindustrialization across America. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Birding Apps Bring More People Into the Wild
items.content: <article>On Bloomberg This Weekend, writer and photographer Alexandra Marvar explains how apps such as Merlin are making birding easier and more accessible, helping draw new people to a hobby that offers an escape into nature. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Marvar also explores whether technology can remove some of the challenge, learning and satisfaction that traditionally come with identifying birds.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Mexico Stresses Sovereignty in US Cooperation
items.content: <article>Mexico’s foreign minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the country maintains a strong relationship with the US while insisting cooperation on security must respect Mexico’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, he says Mexico remains cautiously optimistic about ongoing trade negotiations as it seeks relief from US tariffs on automobiles and steel. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Russia Ukraine War Becomes Economic Battle
items.content: <article>New York Times Kyiv bureau chief Andrew Kramer tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia and Ukraine are increasingly targeting each other’s economies as the war shifts toward attacks on energy, transportation and export infrastructure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kramer says Ukraine is using its expanding drone arsenal to target Russia’s oil industry and its ability to finance a prolonged war. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: McDonald’s Selloff Hits 30% as Big Mac Inflation Spurs Pushback
items.author: Peyton Forte
items.content: <article>McDonald’s Corp. faces a key challenge as it fights to reinvigorate a sagging stock price: Winning back the cost-conscious diners who believe its menu has become too expensive.</article>

items.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
items.content: <article>Campus Moms, smuggling butter, bringing iced coffee to a job interview, and the 'what's for dinner' question: Join Alexis Christoforous, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Higher Bond Yields Mark a Return to Normal
items.content: <article>Ritholtz Wealth Management founder Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that rising bond yields reflect both a normalization of interest rates and inflationary pressures from factors including tariffs and higher energy prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz says higher yields have made fixed income more attractive while investors should consider whether strong equity gains have pushed their portfolios away from their intended allocations. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Northeast Faces Wind, Rain and Coastal Flooding
items.content: <article>Bloomberg News meteorologist Craig Allen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the nor'easter will bring waves of heavy rain and strong winds to the Northeast, along with risks from falling trees, localized flooding and dangerous coastal conditions. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Allen says coastal flooding could affect Long Island, the Jersey Shore, Connecticut and Massachusetts as rough ocean conditions persist through multiple high-tide cycles. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Mideast geoeconomics lead Dina Esfandiary tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a protracted Iran war, marked by cycles of escalation and pauses in fighting, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump-Xi Summit Yields Coal Pledge as Tariff Talks Extend
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US next year and again in 2028, according to the White House, in a sign of progress in easing trade frictions.</article>
